We write everything out completely.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>

Let <MATH_0002> be an <ACCENT_0001>tale covering of <MATH_0003>. If each composition

<MATH_0011> is an <ACCENT_0003>tale morphism, and <MATH_0012> is as in part (3) of
Definition <REF_0001>.
Thus we see that <MATH_0013> has <MATH_0014>.
Conversely, if <MATH_0015> has <MATH_0016> then each <MATH_0017> has
<MATH_0018> by
Definition <REF_0002> part (1).

<STRUCT_0003><STRUCT_0004>

<STRUCT_0007><STRUCT_0008>

<STRUCT_0001>
The following lemma is the analogue of
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0001>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a property of morphisms of schemes which is
<ACCENT_0001>tale local on source-and-target. Let <MATH_0002> be a morphism
of schemes. The following are equivalent:
<STRUCT_0001>
<ITEMOPEN_0001>(a)<ITEMCLOSE_0001> <MATH_0003> has property <MATH_0004>,
<ITEMOPEN_0002>(b)<ITEMCLOSE_0002> for every <MATH_0005> there exists an <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism of germs
<MATH_0006>, an <ACCENT_0003>tale morphism <MATH_0007>, and
a morphism <MATH_0008> such that <MATH_0009> and
<MATH_0010> has <MATH_0011>,
<ITEMOPEN_0003>(c)<ITEMCLOSE_0003>
for any commutative diagram
<MATH_0012>
with <MATH_0013>, <MATH_0014> <ACCENT_0004>tale the morphism <MATH_0015> has <MATH_0016>,
<ITEMOPEN_0004>(d)<ITEMCLOSE_0004> for some diagram as in (c)
with <MATH_0017> surjective <MATH_0018> has <MATH_0019>,
<ITEMOPEN_0005>(e)<ITEMCLOSE_0005> there exists an <ACCENT_0005>tale covering <MATH_0020> such

<STRUCT_0002>

The equivalence of (a) and (b) is part of
Definition <REF_0001>.
The equivalence of (a) and (e) is
Lemma <REF_0002> part (2).
The equivalence of (a) and (f) is
Lemma <REF_0003> part (1).
As (a) is now equivalent to (e) and (f) it follows that
(a) equivalent to (g).

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
It is clear that (c) implies (a). If (a) holds, then for any
diagram as in (c) the morphism <MATH_0001> has <MATH_0002> by
Definition <REF_0004> part (1),
whereupon <MATH_0003> has <MATH_0004> by
Lemma <REF_0005> part (4).
Thus (a) and (c) are equivalent. It is clear that (c) implies (d).
To see that (d) implies (a) assume we have a diagram as in (c)
with <MATH_0005> surjective and <MATH_0006> having <MATH_0007>.
Then <MATH_0008> has <MATH_0009> by
Lemma <REF_0006> part (3).
Since <MATH_0010> is an <ACCENT_0001>tale covering we conclude that
